 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Ric Flair has canceled a scheduled fan appearance in the Seattle area, saying a blood clot in his leg has led his doctors to limit how far he can travel. The WWE Hall of Famer shared the news in a post on X , where he apologized to his agent, Steve Solomon, the Washington State Horror Con, Big Event NY, and his fans in Seattle.
 "Unfortunately, I am dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to 3–4 hours. Seattle falls outside that range, and as disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first," Flair wrote.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Flair pointed to the recent case of Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts as a reason he is taking the issue seriously.
 "Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts and the complications involving blood clots in his lungs. It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly, and I must follow medical advice," he wrote.
 Flair also shared what comes next.
 "I'm scheduled to have a procedure to strip the affected vein, which my doctors expect will allow me to be cleared for more travel afterward," he wrote.
 "Please know this decision was not made lightly. I am truly sorry for the inconvenience and disappointment, and I am incredibly grateful for your patience, understanding, and continued support," Flair added. "I look forward to getting healthy and seeing you all down the road."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This is not the first time the clot has kept Flair from a scheduled appearance in 2026. In August, he missed the Cauliflower Alley Club's 60th reunion in Las Vegas, where he was honored with the Iron Mike Mazurki Award. Jerry Lawler and Jimmy Hart accepted the award on his behalf, and Flair joined by video. "I have a blood clot in my leg, so I can't travel the five or six hour trips that it takes to go to get there," he said. Days later, he flew to Philadelphia for a signing, posting that "a little blood clot is not going to keep me from coming to Philly!"
 The 77-year-old has dealt with several serious health problems over the past decade. The most frightening came in August 2017, when he was rushed to the hospital with severe abdominal pain. Flair spent about 10 days on life support in a medically induced coma, doctors removed part of his bowel and inserted a pacemaker, and his family was told he had about a 20 percent chance of survival. Flair later said years of drinking nearly cost him his life.
 In May 2019, Flair was hospitalized again in Atlanta due to what his wife at the time, Wendy Barlow, described as ongoing health complications. He underwent a heart procedure in which he received a new pacemaker and had a blood clot treated.
 Flair returned to the ring for his final match in July 2022. In 2024, he said he had suffered a heart attack during the match without realizing it, and that he learned of it after a doctor's visit and tests in late 2023.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In 2025, Flair announced that he was battling skin cancer for the second time in about three years. "Melanoma, I have found out, is nothing to play with," he wrote at the time. He pulled out of a fan meet-and-greet in Mississippi in June 2025 after his doctors advised him not to travel, and in July, he announced that he was cancer-free following treatment.
